# Bucket B rate decomposition

## 1. What the 29 measured cycles actually bought

Source: `docs/release/SD-34-book-completion/artifacts/epic-3-core-rulebook/step-cost-ledger.json` `.buckets_cleared_so_far.B` and its per-commit backing `step-cost-ledger-raw-commits.json` (re-derived here by filtering the 29 `AT-34-E3-001`-tagged commits + the 1 `merge: tranche/14` reconciliation commit the ledger's own `mechanism_breakdown` counts as a B cycle). My per-cycle re-aggregation reproduces the ledger's own totals exactly: 503 net units left bucket B (denominator: 970 starting core_rulebook bucket-B population) across 2432.3 wall-minutes (40.54h), of which 235 reached DONE and 268 were reclassified to D/V/X/M — MEASURED, n=29 cycles, one book.

## 2. The slow tail is real and it is NOT one thing

Splitting those same 29 cycles by mechanism *shape* (not by wall-time bucket) — generic/table/fallback/predicate-batch mechanisms vs. owner-matched/live-probe/per-unit-judgment mechanisms — and re-summing wall-minutes and units per class reproduces the ledger totals exactly (503 units, 2432.3 min, 235 DONE), so the split is internally consistent, not curve-fit:

| class | cycles | units left B | wall-min | wall-hr | units/hr (net-B) | units reaching DONE | DONE/hr |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **FAST** (generic/table/fallback/predicate, batch-shaped) | 14 | 451 (89.7% of 503) | 795.2 | 13.25 | 34.03 | 194 (82.6% of 235) | **14.64** |
| **SLOW** (owner-matched / live-probe / per-unit judgment) | 15 | 52 (10.3% of 503) | 1637.1 | 27.29 | 1.91 | 41 (17.4% of 235) | **1.50** |

Blended DONE-rate = 235/40.54h = 5.797 ≈ the ledger's own stated 5.8 units/hr — confirms the split is a correct decomposition of the official number, not a competing measurement. MEASURED, n=29 cycles / 503 units / 235 DONE units, core_rulebook only.

**The asymmetry is the whole story:** the fast class does 90% of the throughput in 33% of the wall time; the slow class does 10% of the throughput and eats 67% of the wall time. Fast is ~9.8x faster than slow measured on DONE/hr (14.64 vs 1.50), ~17.8x on raw net-B-clearing/hr (34.03 vs 1.91).

**What the fast cycles were** (examples, all `step-cost-ledger-raw-commits.json`): `04377a287d` — a generic `race_trait_generic/` table fallback cleared 132 units in 70.0 min (113/hr); `ae0f387dd3` — a reusable "Shape 7" book-wide grant cleared 72 units in 45.2 min (95.6/hr); `cb0ba2286e` — a verified-predicate batch classification cleared 93 units in 93.5 min (59.7/hr); `c3202a90ce` — a generic Bonus-record shape (Favored Enemy/Terrain) cleared 42 units in 56.1 min (44.9/hr). Time was spent building/wiring ONE mechanism that then swept many records at once.

**What the slow cycles were**: the two most expensive cycles in the whole ledger are both this class — `30fa0e6653` (617.4 min, 2 units, 0.19/hr): the receipt (`AT-34-E3-001_class_feature_option_pool_with_magnitude_cycle_receipt_9.md`) shows the time going into widening a live probe (`probe_fighter_weapon_training_wiring`) to cover all 56 (tier,group) combinations against the real fixture and re-verifying against the engine's own pre-existing formula — genuine per-shape verification engineering, not typing; and `49d72f5e03` (253.6 min, 3 units, 0.71/hr, "owner-matched cycle 6" grounding Cleric/Assassin/Shadowdancer weapon-and-armor proficiency) plus three sibling owner-matched cycles (`0302b44ae8`, `eff925305f`, and the pattern repeats) — each is a per-class manual proficiency/scope verification that does not batch because each class's rules text differs. `9a0d75a9b7`, `1de361c850`, `df94dd024c`, `6a87278d87` are the same shape one level down: per-school live grounding, one Wizard school per cycle, non-batchable because each school's spell list and formula differ.

**Classification: engine-addressable vs intrinsically manual.** The fast class is engine-addressable by construction — it IS the class where building one generic mechanism (a table-fallback, a book-wide grant shape, a verified predicate) cleared a double-digit-to-triple-digit unit count in a single cycle. The slow class is, on the evidence read, intrinsically manual for a materially different reason than "nobody built the tool yet": owner-matched and per-school/per-class cycles require reading that class's/school's *specific* rules text and verifying it against the engine's live computed output one class/school at a time — the bottleneck is judgment against non-uniform source text, not missing automation. The one partial counter-example is `8e7aecc855`/`f98c6abddc` (decomposition into 7 named sub-causes, multi-DESC ingest truncation) — this looks like it COULD become engine-addressable once the sub-causes are individually enumerated and batched, but SD-34 has not yet done that enumeration, so it is classified SLOW here on the evidence actually in hand, not assumed permanently manual.

## 3. A caution the ultimate_campaign sample raises

`artifacts/epic-4-ultimate-campaign/step-cost-ledger.json` `.buckets_cleared_so_far.B`: its one bucket-B cycle explicitly **reused an already-built generic mechanism** ("decisions.md §14 PI-coordinate wire-up ... already built for Kind::Domain/Kind::Deity") yet still ran at 1.667 units/hr (5 units, 108 min) — the SLOW end of the official range, not the fast end. n=1, and forward-plan.json's own caveat calls this a sample-size artifact, but it is the only cross-book data point that exists, and it points the same direction as the doctrine already on file: bucket A's caveat (`forward-plan.json .measured_rates.A`) that a table/mechanism BUILD cost is separate from and does not eliminate a per-unit/per-book WIRING cost. Rolling a fast mechanism out to a NEW book still pays a per-book setup tax before its marginal rate applies — this session's within-book fast/slow split is a POST-setup-cost figure, and I found no measurement of that per-book setup tax's size. MEASURED (n=1) but explicitly flagged non-generalizable by its own source.

## 4. Answering the question: what fraction of bucket B's 11,299 units plausibly moves fast vs stays slow

Denominator throughout: bucket B's population-wide remaining count is **11,299** units, out of SD-35's 29,283-unit remainder (`forward-plan.json` `.population.remaining_by_bucket.B`; the 35-book, non-vehicle-book population).

Applying the MEASURED core_rulebook unit-count mix (89.7% fast-shaped / 10.3% slow-shaped, n=503 units, one book) to the population-wide 11,299 is an **EXTRAPOLATION**, not a measurement — I have exactly one within-book decomposition and one thin (n=1) cross-book data point that argues the marginal rate is NOT guaranteed to transfer without its own setup cost. With that caveat stated plainly:

- **EXTRAPOLATED, ~10,135 units (≈89.7% of 11,299)** are shaped like the fast class — generic table/fallback/predicate/book-wide-grant mechanisms — and plausibly clear near the MEASURED fast DONE-rate of 14.64 units/hr *if* the equivalent generic mechanism is built and wired into each new book (paying its own per-book/per-kind setup cost, whose size is a genuine measurement gap — see below). At that rate: ~692 engineering hours for this slice alone.
- **EXTRAPOLATED, ~1,164 units (≈10.3% of 11,299)** are shaped like the slow class — owner-matched / live-probe / per-school-or-per-class judgment — and no plausible engine investment moves them off the MEASURED slow DONE-rate of 1.50 units/hr, because the bottleneck is reading and verifying non-uniform per-class/per-school source text, not missing tooling. At that rate: ~776 engineering hours for this slice.
- Summed: **~1,468 EXTRAPOLATED engineering hours** for bucket B corpus-wide if the fast/slow mix and rates transfer as measured — well below the naive blended-rate range of 1,948.1-6,778.0h (`forward-plan.json` sum of `.books[].buckets.B.projected_cost_hours_range`, which applies the single blended 1.667-5.8/hr figure uniformly and is explicitly flagged by the plan itself as a single-point misrepresentation). This is directionally supported, not proven, by `forward-scope-register.md` §C1.5's MEASURED corpus-wide finding that 29 of 136 distinct mechanisms cover 90% of all non-DONE units and that a generic mechanism built once (Epic 2's tables) demonstrably swept 8,463→449 of the corpus-wide bucket-A population in ~4 cycles — real evidence that mechanism concentration and cross-book leverage exist in this corpus, though that finding is bucket-A-specific and corpus-wide-mechanism-general, not bucket-B-specific.
- **ASSUMED**: that the OTHER 34 books' bucket-B mechanism composition resembles core_rulebook's 89.7/10.3 split at all. No book-by-book bucket-B mechanism inventory exists in the read artifacts (`forward-plan.json` gives each book only a single blended B rate, not a mechanism breakdown) — this is the load-bearing assumption behind the whole extrapolation, and the ultimate_campaign n=1 sample is the only other data point, and it does not confirm the split.

**Bottom line for the scary 28x number**: it is not evidence that bucket B is uniformly hard. It is the ledger correctly refusing to average over two regimes that measure 9.8-17.8x apart. On the unit-count evidence in hand, the regime that dominates population-wide (fast, ~90% of units) is the one that responds to engine investment; the regime that is genuinely resistant (slow, ~10% of units) is resistant because of source-text non-uniformity, not tooling absence — and it still drives roughly half the projected wall time even at 10% of the units.

gaps: No per-book, per-mechanism bucket-B breakdown exists for the 34 books beyond core_rulebook and ultimate_campaign (forward-plan.json gives only one blended rate per book) -- the 89.7%/10.3% fast/slow mix is measured for one book and extrapolated corpus-wide with no cross-book confirmation.

The per-book/per-kind SETUP cost of wiring an already-built generic bucket-B mechanism into a NEW book (distinct from the mechanism's own build cost, and distinct from its marginal per-unit rate once wired) is not measured anywhere I could read -- ultimate_campaign's n=1 sample (reused mechanism, still ran at the slow end) suggests this cost is non-trivial but n=1 cannot size it.

AT-34-E3-001_class_feature_option_pool_record_not_held_by_engine's 7 decomposed sub-causes were never individually re-measured after decomposition (receipt notes partial closure 63->57 then stops) -- whether that whole family reclassifies from SLOW to FAST once each sub-cause is batched is unresolved.

I did not run scripts/completion_atlas.py or any generator (read-only mandate); all bucket-B figures above are as committed in step-cost-ledger.json / step-cost-ledger-raw-commits.json / forward-plan.json and were cross-checked only by re-aggregating those same committed numbers, not by re-deriving from docs/work-inventory.json at HEAD.
